pathogen.value: Duck hepatitis virus types 1, 1a, 2 and 3 (DHV-1 is an enterovirus, DHV-2 an astrovirus, DHV-3 a picornavirus)

value: spreads rapidly within a flock of young ducklings
weakness or paralysis of the legs

mortality.value: DHV-1 is highly virulent, with death occurring within 1-2 hours of signs appearing in young ducklings under 6 weeks old

diagnosis.value: based on clinical signs and post-mortem exam showing an enlarged, greenish liver with bleeding spots; confirmed by lab virus testing

value: strict isolation of ducklings in their first 4-5 weeks of life
disinfecting the environment with phenol or formaldehyde

treatment_overview.value: no effective treatment once a duckling is infected

summary.value: Duck hepatitis virus is a fast-killing viral disease of young ducklings that damages the liver and can cause death within hours of the first signs. It is specific to ducks, does not infect humans, and is prevented mainly through vaccination and strict isolation of young birds.
